items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: Went back to Pittsburgh and I joined that band

ctx.x: And was this fella Dick Stabile —

Yeah. Dick Stabile — there was a trumpet player from Buffalo by the name of Joe Gustafaro, who — which, Dick was leaving the band and of course the news got around. And my brother drove me to Pittsburgh to, in essence, audition. All I did was Dick said,

“What do you want to play?” And I said, “Confessing.” I played a chorus of “Confessing,” and he said all right, but you can’t — I was playing cornet — he said, “You can’t play on this you’ve got to get a trumpet. We drove clear back to Buffalo to a music store and got me a trumpet. Went back to Pittsburgh and I joined that band and that’s how, through that band, when we were working in Cleveland, Red Norvo’s band came. Mr. and Mrs. Swing came in to work the theater. And living at the Allerton Hotel in Cleveland,…
